headline: High-risk shared-state Dify pair: default workspace and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write files, run tools, and shares state via the Dify server datastore, so agent_b can plausibly feed content back into agent_a through a shared workspace or orchestration path. nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress but no documented isolation or provenance controls. The pathway is inferred, not directly documented, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF agent_b can write content into the shared Dify datastore or uploaded files
IF agent_a later parses that content as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Disable shared datastore access between instances for this pair
Require provenance tags on all inter-agent content
Route agent_b outputs through a human review step
Restrict agent_a to read-only access for untrusted inputs
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping middleware

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a explicitly touches knowledge base content and conversation logs and can write/read files with broad network egress; agent_b has allowlisted egress but no stated local-only guarantee. If they share a workspace or datastore, sensitive content from agent_a can flow into agent_b outputs or outbound requests. The shared-workspace pathway is plausible but not fully documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents access the same Dify datastore or filesystem
IF agent_b forwards received content to an external endpoint within its allowlist
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials per agent
Remove sensitive data from shared prompts and files
Turn off broad egress for agent_a where possible
Review outbound allowlist for agent_b
requires-engineering: implement per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, read/write the filesystem, and use broad network egress; agent_b has allowlisted network egress. Even without explicit write overlap for agent_b, both can act on shared mutable resources if orchestrated together, creating coordination conflicts. Because agent_b lacks documented filesystem write, I do not escalate to high, but the shared-state model keeps this in medium.
conditions: IF both agents are granted access to the same mutable workspace or API credentials
IF the orchestrator does not enforce locking or turn-taking
mitigations: Assign separate credentials and directories
Serialize writes through a single coordinator
Disable shell execution for untrusted tasks
Audit shared mutable resources before deployment
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an agent/workflow platform that can pass outputs into downstream tools, and agent_a can generate tool-using workflows; agent_b is a scientific-research agent with no documented verification barrier. That makes it plausible that agent_b treats agent_a output as authoritative. The interaction is inferred from profiles rather than directly evidenced, so medium is safer than low.
conditions: IF agent_a output is used as input to agent_b without an explicit verification step
IF agent_b acts on agent_a-produced facts or citations
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents
Require source citations before downstream action
Limit agent_a to drafting, not deciding
Have agent_b cross-check against independent sources
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a touches conversation logs and knowledge base content and may handle model-provider API keys and tool credentials, while agent_b has no documented sensitive-data classes or residency constraints. No direct compliance mismatch is documented, so only a low-risk gap exists if regulated data is placed into agent_a and then forwarded. The other agent is not cited for a specific mismatch because its profile lacks compliance fields.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in agent_a's conversation logs or knowledge base
IF that data is then exported to a jurisdiction or service not approved for it
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared prompts
Review retention settings for conversation logs
Restrict secrets to dedicated vaults
Document data-handling boundaries
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
